note: Generated from each plugins/<name>/profile.ttl. Do not edit; run npm run build:index.

plugins.label: 8-Bit 8asterd
plugins.comment: Three AY-3-8910 chips under the 8b8 firmware, running unmodified as WebAssembly. Nine voices across three chips, hardware envelopes, a percussion set on channel 10, and the firmware's own vibrato, tremolo, arpeggiator, buzzy bass, circuit bending and ten tuning temperaments.
cautions: Nine voices across three chips, and the tenth note steals the oldest rather than being refused. Percussion and pitched notes come out of the same nine.
Percussion is MIDI channel 10, notes 35 to 59. Pitched notes are 24 to 96 on any other channel, and anything outside that is ignored rather than transposed into range.
Every control answers to a MIDI CC as well, from CC 70 upward in parameter order, which is what the hardware does. A host automating a parameter and a controller sending its CC will fight.
Roll and Retrigger are positions on an exponential curve from about 1.5Hz to 45Hz rather than a rate in hertz. The figure shown is the one the device's own panel shows.
The firmware's EEPROM is a scratch array that is never persisted. Its SAVE command has nowhere to write, and settings belong in the project graph instead.

plugins.label: BassGen
plugins.comment: Transport synced bass line generator. Scale, genre and subdivision shape a seeded pattern that plays in time with the session and can be steered from a keyboard.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Monophonic by design. A new step ends the note before it rather than overlapping.

plugins.label: Boost
plugins.comment: A gain stage in C++, the minimal starting point for a WebAssembly JigDAW plugin: everything in boost.cpp beyond jig_process is ABI wiring, meant to be copied.

plugins.label: Cadence
plugins.comment: Transport synced MIDI harmonizer that learns a chord cycle from what it hears and plays voiced progressions with comping in time with the session.
cautions: Silent until it has learned a cycle: play notes into it while the transport rolls, and it starts harmonizing at the next cycle boundary.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. Learn is a trigger that fires on the rising edge.
With pass_input on, incoming notes continue downstream alongside the harmony.

plugins.label: Cascade
plugins.comment: Schroeder plate reverb with per-mode scaling, damping inside the feedback loop, and a freeze that holds the tail indefinitely.
cautions: Freeze holds the tail at unity feedback. Following it with a limiter is wise when several instances are frozen at once.

plugins.label: DrumGen
plugins.comment: Transport synced MIDI drum generator. Genre, style mode and resolution shape a seeded pattern that plays in time with the session, with fills on the last bar of the loop and Conductor CC control.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to a drum instrument. New, Mutate and Fill are triggers that fire on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
A held note with no note off is a stuck note, so stopping the transport sounds the ringing notes now rather than leaving them held.

plugins.label: DrumKit
plugins.comment: Eleven voice synthesised drum instrument. MIDI notes trigger the voices, the master bus adds crush, drive and room, and per-instrument mutes cut voices immediately.
cautions: One-shot voices: note-offs do nothing, and a hit cannot be choked except the open hat, which a closed hat cuts short.
CC 120 and 123 reset every voice and the master bus, like an all-notes-off.
The eleven trig outputs the native wrapper exposes as UI LEDs are not parameters here and have no panel control.

plugins.label: Dynamix
plugins.comment: Compressor/expander, limiter and clipper/soft distortion in series. A second stereo input on channels 3 and 4 is an external key: when it is connected, the compressor/expander stage reads its level from that instead of the main signal, for sidechain ducking. When nothing is connected there, the stage detects on the main signal itself.
cautions: The limiter has no lookahead: it reacts within a fraction of a millisecond rather than before the transient, so a very sharp attack can still touch the ceiling briefly before the gain catches up. Leave a little headroom below the ceiling for material with hard transients.

The compressor/expander stage links its gain reduction across both channels from a single detected level, so it never shifts the stereo image, but it also means the side chain input's balance between its own two channels, not just its overall level, feeds the detector.
Disconnecting the side chain input mid-session returns the compressor/expander to detecting on the main signal on the next block, not instantly at the sample the cable was pulled.

plugins.label: Ferrite
plugins.comment: A neural amp model (nam-rs, MIT, ported from and validated against the reference Python and C++ implementations) in series with an impulse response, a cabinet or a room of up to 2.7 seconds, by partitioned FFT convolution. The amp can be switched off to use it as a convolution reverb, and Mix blends the convolved signal with the dry one. Ships a small example .nam and a synthetic (not captured) cabinet IR; both jig:asset resources are meant to be replaced with your own.
cautions: The neural model and the cabinet impulse response are both loaded at the sample rate they were captured or trained at, 48 kHz for the example model here. This plugin does not resample: a host running at a different rate gets a load that reports a mismatch (see the module's own jig_load_nam and jig_load_ir return codes) rather than silently wrong output.
The shipped impulse response is synthetic, generated for this example, not a real cabinet capture.
One amp model, run on the mean of both input channels: an amp is a mono device, and a real capture is too heavy to run twice.
Impulse responses are normalised to unit energy, so a response sets the tone and not the level. Stereo responses are mixed to mono.
Needs WebAssembly SIMD, which every current browser has. The native adapter's interpreter does not, and could not run a real capture in real time if it did.

plugins.label: Ground
plugins.comment: Transport synced long-form bass generator. Form shapes and phrase roles plan a whole section that plays in time with the session, with arc tension and Conductor control including scene-driven role overrides.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to a bass instrument. New Form, New Phrase and Mutate Cell are triggers that fire on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
Monophonic by design. A new note ends the note before it rather than overlapping.

plugins.label: JigDAW Gain Trim
plugins.comment: Converted by bin/jsfx-import.js from examples/jsfx/gain-trim.jsfx, a REAPER JSFX effect, and run under the shared interpreter in plugins/_jsfx-runtime/.
cautions: Converted from JSFX by a restricted EEL2 subset: no user-defined function, no strings, no gmem, and while()/loop() are bounded so a runaway script goes silent rather than missing the audio thread's deadline. See plugins/_jsfx-runtime/README.md.

plugins.label: MelGen
plugins.comment: Transport synced phrase-aware melody generator. Period, contour and answer shape a seeded line that plays in time with the session, follows an incoming line when asked, and answers Conductor CCs.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. New, Notes and Rhythm are triggers that fire on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
Monophonic by design. A new note ends the note before it rather than overlapping.

plugins.label: Pulse
plugins.comment: Eight voice subtractive synthesiser with saw, square and triangle oscillators, a one-pole lowpass and an attack-release envelope.
cautions: Eight voices. A ninth note steals the oldest voice rather than being refused.

plugins.label: Quefrency
plugins.comment: Separates its input through the cepstrum into a formant envelope and a harmonic structure, shifts and reshapes each independently, and multiplies them back together.
cautions: Latency is 2047 frames at 50 kHz and below, and 4095 above. The processor reports the figure for the actual rate; the module ABI carries no latency, so a native host is not told it and will not compensate.
The formant envelope of a chord is the envelope of the whole mixture. Pitch shift moves every spectral peak, so chords stay chords, but it cannot act on one note of a chord alone.
Transients smear when pitch or frequency shift is set, as with any phase vocoder.
Lifter must sit below the shortest pitch period in the input, or harmonics leak into the formant envelope and move with it.

MIDI control changes 70 to 80, on any channel, drive the parameters in the order Formant shift, Formant depth, Formant tilt per octave, Pitch shift, Pitch fine, Frequency shift, Harmonic depth, Lifter, Envelope estimator, Mix, Output. Value 64 is each parameter's default where the default lies inside its range, so a centred controller changes nothing; 64 and above selects the true envelope.
A controller's value is not shown on the panel and is not saved with the project. It holds until the host's own value for that parameter next changes, and then the host's value wins.

plugins.label: Squelch
plugins.comment: A resonant lowpass filter whose cutoff an envelope follower pushes up on every note, for the acid bass sweep. Put it after a synth: each note opens the filter and Decay sets how fast it closes. Plain JavaScript, no WebAssembly module.
cautions: Resonance stops short of self-oscillation, and the output is soft clipped to keep a note on the resonant peak from being much louder than the rest.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: Tremolo
plugins.comment: Amplitude modulation by a sine LFO. Its whole signal path is JavaScript: no WebAssembly module, the worked example for a plugin whose processing does not need one.
cautions: Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.
